author: yevbar

release_rule: reallocated by push and released by parser_free after each occupied jv slot is released by parser_reset
author: yevbar

release_rule: new containers and object keys are transferred into stack slots; ordinary nested member values move from next into the array or object held by a stack slot; parser_reset releases remaining occupied slots, while closing containers move from stack into next
author: yevbar

release_rule: streaming initialization allocates it; reset releases and replaces it, and parser_free releases the final path
author: yevbar

release_rule: streaming completion transfers it to the caller or slices it into a returned value plus retained follow-up state; reset releases any remainder
author: yevbar

release_rule: value stores accepted input in next; ordinary parsing moves keys to stack, nested member values into stack-held containers, and closing containers back into next; ordinary completion transfers a top-level next to the caller, streaming moves next into path or output records later transferred to the caller, and reset releases any remainder
author: yevbar

release_rule: tokenadd reallocates it as needed and parser_free releases it; completed tokens reuse the allocation after resetting tokenpos
author: yevbar

release_rule: parser_init initializes it and parser_free releases it
author: yevbar

release_rule: jv_parser_new allocates the parser; caller must pass it to jv_parser_free, which releases internal state and the parser allocation
author: yevbar

owner: jv_parser.next, then parser-owned stack, container, path, or output; caller at completion
release_rule: value releases val when rejecting a separator conflict; otherwise it stores val in next, from which ordinary parsing transfers object keys to stack and nested member values into the enclosing stack-held array or object before top-level completion transfers next to the caller, while streaming transfers keys into path and values into output records; parser reset releases any retained parser-owned destination after error
author: yevbar

release_rule: the parser moves next into out and replaces its slot with invalid
author: yevbar

release_rule: the parser constructs output with a path copy and moved next, or transfers/slices output while retaining only explicitly scheduled follow-up state
author: yevbar

release_rule: the formatted string is transferred into either a stream-error array or an invalid message value; the caller receiving jv_parser_next must release it
author: yevbar

release_rule: valid values and message-bearing invalids transfer ownership to the caller; a message-bearing invalid allocates a refcounted jvp_invalid that owns its error message and releases both on final free, while jv_invalid returns the immediate zero-pointer JV_INVALID value with no allocation
author: yevbar

release_rule: extra-value and later-error paths release superseded values; parser state is always freed before the final value is returned
author: yevbar

class: borrowed sized buffer with NUL-accessible backing
release_rule: jv_parser_set_buf scans at most length bytes, but after parser_free every message-bearing invalid result is decorated by passing string as a %s argument through jv_string_fmt and jv_string_vfmt to vsnprintf; the caller must keep the backing valid throughout the call and ensure a NUL is reachable from string within accessible backing, normally at string[length]; an earlier embedded NUL truncates only the decorated input text, not the length-bounded parse
author: yevbar

release_rule: jv_dump_term recursively consumes x and releases it at the end of the term; jv_dumpf, jv_dump, and jv_dump_string transfer their input into that operation
author: yevbar

release_rule: sorted and native iteration return owned key copies; each key is released immediately after printing
author: yevbar

release_rule: object iteration returns an owned value copy and recursive jv_dump_term consumes it
author: yevbar

release_rule: sorted output creates the key array on first iteration and releases it after its final index
author: yevbar

release_rule: the procedure allocates an output jv string, transfers the consumed input through jv_dump_term, and returns the output to the caller
author: yevbar

release_rule: append replaces the slot with the returned string value; the enclosing jv_dump_string returns that final owned value
author: yevbar

release_rule: jq_set_colors frees it for an empty configuration or reallocates it for each valid non-empty configuration; either transition invalidates or moves prior colors[] aliases
author: yevbar

release_rule: entries alias static defaults or slices inside colors_buf and are rewritten after colors_buf is freed or reallocated; they must not be freed independently or retained across configuration changes
author: yevbar

release_rule: jv_dump_string consumes x, the truncation helper releases the temporary rendered string, and caller retains ownership of the supplied output buffer
author: yevbar

release_rule: the function writes and NUL-terminates within the supplied buffer and returns the same pointer without taking ownership
author: yevbar

release_rule: the API records a possibly BOM-advanced alias into the caller buffer and allocates no replacement storage
author: yevbar

release_rule: parse errors release the provisional output, then parser_reset releases path/output/next/stack values and preserves reusable allocated buffers until parser_free
author: yevbar

release_rule: jv_show passes a refcounted copy to jv_dumpf, so printer consumption releases the copy while the caller retains its input
author: yevbar

release_rule: opening brackets and braces transfer fresh containers into stack slots; closing transfers the top slot into next; parser_reset releases every still-occupied slot and parser_free releases stack storage
author: yevbar

release_rule: value transfers an accepted scalar into next; comma or a matching closer transfers it into the current container and invalidates next; a separator conflict releases the rejected incoming value
author: yevbar

release_rule: array set transfers the incoming value into one slot after releasing the displaced owner; final backing release walks and releases every initialized element exactly once
author: yevbar
